news.titleTr: Are Alt-L1s over? Security, costs drive smaller chains to Ethereum
news.summaryTr: L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist.
news.articleText: Are Alt-L1s over? Security, costs drive smaller chains to Ethereum L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist. Running an independent blockchain has always come with a particular promise: control. A standalone Layer 1 architecture allows projects to be the masters of their own destiny, set the rules of consensus, maintain their own validators and build infrastructure around their users, without relying on any other network. But with great power comes great responsibility — and considerable expense. Blockchains need enough users, developers and economic activity to support the infrastructure that secures them. For some smaller networks, keeping an entire ecosystem afloat no longer makes economic sense. Zilliqa is the latest project to confront that reality, announcing plans last week to move away from its L1 architecture and become an Ethereum-based Layer 2 (L2) instead: “We know it’s not great. For nine years we built and ran our own Layer 1. It hasn’t worked.” “Usage never reached what a standalone chain needs,” the post explained. “Funding and liquidity for standalone L1s dried up. The recent hacks showed how much it takes to secure a chain alone. The data is onchain for everyone to see.” Zilliqa is not alone. Blockchain ecosystem Gnosis (which has always been Ethereum-adjacent) is also working to transition Gnosis Chain into an Ethereum-based network through its Ethereum Economic Zone (EEZ) initiative. Its RollupX test network intends to show how participating chains can share Ethereum settlement and synchronous composability as native rollups. Gaming-focused Ronin blockchain also completed its move back to Ethereum as an L2 in May. With interest in alt L1s drying up along with the funding, will we start to see more and more chains consolidating in the Ethereum ecosystem? The cost of going it alone Independent L1s generally have to keep several core functions going, including execution, consensus, data availability and settlement. They must also fund the token incentives used to secure their networks through staking. Related: What are native rollups? Full guide to Ethereum’s latest innovation “It comes down to a chain’s profitability,” Max Shannon, senior research analyst at Bitwise, tells Magazine. ZIL becomes a Layer 2 on Ethereum. Source: Zilliqa “L2s only need to maintain execution and do not necessarily need a token, which makes them a more attractive financial and operational proposition,” he says. Shannon says the top ten largest projects are more financially sustainable. Coinbase and Robinhood’s L2 networks generated $48 million and $52 million in fees respectively over the last 365 days, with margins above 90%. The next eight largest chains each generated more than $1 million annually. From 11th place onward, however, annual fees collectively amounted to less than $1 million. So a network may have ambitious technology and a dedicated community, but those things don’t necessarily pay the bills. Ethereum is often criticized for giving away too much of its revenue to L2s, but that’s precisely what makes it attractive to set up projects there. But just becoming an Ethereum L2 doesn’t automatically make a network profitable however. Shannon points to Optimism, Katana and Linea as examples of networks whose expenses outweigh their fee revenue. Projects like Blast have already been forced to shut down. Ethereum as a liquidity ‘black hole’ Gnosis has targeted spring 2027 to complete its transition, which will see it give up its independent validator-based consensus in favor of Ethereum settlement. Gnosis Chain will relaunch as an Ethereum Economic Zone. Source: Gnosis “Two years ago I gave a talk about ‘native Rollups’ that would truly extend Ethereum instead of being isolated chains,” co-founder Martin Köppelmann said, adding that RollupX “even goes beyond what I had imagined back then!” Gnosis’s EEZ initiative aims to enable separate Ethereum-based networks interact synchronously, so a smart contract on one network can call another and use its response within the same transaction, without relying on the usual bridge-and-wait process. That’s a prospect that has some Ethereum supporters particularly bullish, with ETH bull materkel describing the EEZ as a potential “black hole for liquidity,” and saying it could allow participating networks to tap into Ethereum’s total value locked (TVL) and strengthen its position as a liquidity hub. Could network effects, and increased interoperability draw more and more chains into Ethereum’s orbit? Beyond the cost savings It isn’t only the operating cost economics that make sense. Projects can also tap into an established ecosystem of applications and developers rather than building those network effects from scratch. Related: Privacy tools are rising behind institutional adoption, says ZKsync dev Alex Gluchowski, co-founder and chief executive of Matter Labs, the company behind Ethereum L2 ZKsync, says he expects more L1 teams to maintain their own chains while using Ethereum for settlement. “Running an independent L1 means maintaining its security as well as building something people want to use,” Gluchowski tells Magazine. “Sharing Ethereum’s security gives a team more room to focus on its users. I see very few user needs that require an independent L1 rather than an Ethereum-based chain.” But Gluchowski says sovereignty and Ethereum integration are not mutually exclusive, since chains can retain control over their rules and operations while using Ethereum for shared settlement. Ronin completed migration to Ethereum in May. Source: Ronin And for applications handling sensitive financial information, maintaining a private environment under their own control can be essential, he says. Shared settlement does not have to mean exposing confidential transaction data. The biggest obstacle today is that all the L2s are effectively isolated from each other and from Ethereum. It’s certainly possible to jump between them, but its far from seamless and interoperability is poor. “Fragmentation is already happening,” Gluchowski says, pointing to the difficulty of connecting networks when transactions involve privacy. Interoperability between private environments will become more important as more applications seek to combine confidential activity with access to public blockchain liquidity, he says. Does every chain need Ethereum? Shannon cautions against describing the market as undergoing straightforward consolidation around Ethereum. Some large institutions are launching L2 networks, he says, including Coinbase and Robinhood, but others are still choosing to build independent L1s, like Circle’s Arc, Stripe’s Tempo, or Hyperliquid’s purpose-specific perpetual futures blockchain. “So there is no clear conclusion to the L1 versus L2 debate as yet,” he says. news.title: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
news.summary: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
news.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
news.titleTr: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
news.summaryTr: The UK is seeing impressive growth, but will it last?
news.articleText: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient - Published The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September. "Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy. It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War". Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth. It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity. The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic. The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%. Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago. This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France. It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise. Not a boom While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either. Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helping to boost growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes. While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week. Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment. I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss. However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year. Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again. There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed. The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf. Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too. Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy". - Published6 days ago - Published5 hours ago

news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements
news.articleText: Release Number 9322-26 CFTC Staff Addresses Use of Trust Companies for Daily Settlements November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s Division of Clearing and Risk today issued a no-action letter addressing whether derivatives clearing organizations may use trust companies to conduct daily settlements with clearing members. According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading
news.articleText: Release Number 9318-26 CFTC to Host Roundtable on 24/7 Trading October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced it will host an industry roundtable Dec. 15 to discuss issues related to the viability of derivatives markets moving to 24/7 trading. The dialogue will build upon the CFTC’s Request for Comment earlier this summer on 24/7 trading. The CFTC’s roundtable will provide a public venue for dialogue on the evolving market structures shaping derivatives markets, including overnight trading, tokenization, infrastructure and staffing needs, and operational readiness. Participants will convene from across the industry to discuss how the Commission can promote responsible innovation while protecting market participants and preserving the integrity and resilience of U.S. derivatives markets. “I have been consistently clear: under my leadership, the CFTC will not take a one‑size‑fits‑all approach to 24/7 trading. Market structure evolves best through thoughtful and responsible progress, and that’s exactly why we’re hosting a roundtable to hear directly from industry on their views for 24/7 trading across different asset classes,” Chairman Selig said. The roundtable will take place at CFTC’s headquarters in Washington. Information regarding the agenda, speakers, and registration will be posted at a later date. This event will be open to the public and livestreamed on CFTC.gov. Please note the number of in-person participants may be limited, and visitors will be subject to security checks. Members of the public are welcome to submit speaker nominations to [email protected]. -CFTC-

news.title: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026
news.articleText: Release Number 9317-26 ICYMI: Agricultural Leaders and Market Participants Join CFTC Chairman Selig in Overland Park, Kansas for AgCon 2026 October 27, 2026 WASHINGTON — Last week, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the Risk Management Center at Kansas State University co-hosted the 2026 Agricultural Commodity Futures Conference (AgCon) in Overland Park, Kansas. The two-day conference brought together industry leaders, policymakers, and market participants to examine critical issues facing the agricultural economy, developments in derivatives markets, and the risk management tools American farmers, ranchers, and agribusinesses depend on. Conference Highlights CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig joined K-State President Richard Linton to welcome participants on opening day. CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig addressed conference attendees, “I have spent a lot of time this year traveling around the country and talking to farmers and ranchers working hard each day to provide the food, feed, and fiber we depend on throughout our country and the world. I’ve met with farmers, ranchers, agribusinesses, and energy producers in Iowa, Texas, Nebraska, South Carolina, and Florida, and now, I’m with all of you here in Kansas.” [Watch Chairman Selig’s full remarks here.] Following Chairman Selig’s remarks, panelists examined the relationship between cash and derivatives markets, evolving commodity contracts, and the importance of effective hedging tools for agricultural producers. There were also panels where industry representatives addressed access to agricultural credit and the financial challenges facing producers and merchants. Additional afternoon discussions focused on rising production costs, fluctuating commodity prices, supply chain disruptions, and broader pressures on the farm economy. In addition, conference participants engaged in discussions about emerging market developments, including perpetual futures, 24/7 trading, and tokenized collateral, and their implications for agricultural risk management. CFTC Chief Advisor Alex Titus and White House Council of Economic Advisers Member Aaron Hedlund also examined the U.S. economic outlook, agricultural trade, and policies shaping American agriculture. The first day concluded with a keynote address from U.S. Department of Agriculture Deputy Secretary Stephen Vaden. U.S. Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas opened the second day with a morning keynote address on agricultural policy and legislative priorities facing American producers. The morning continued with discussions on agricultural prediction markets, the use of data in modern commodity markets, and developments in event contracts. In addition, panelists examined superintelligence, information advantages, and market integrity, including the implications of emerging technologies for market participants and regulators. Chairman Selig joined Futures Industry Association President and CEO Walt Lukken for a fireside chat examining the Commission’s priorities, the evolving regulatory landscape, and developments shaping derivatives markets. The conference concluded with discussions on enhancing public understanding of markets through data and customer education, followed by a panel examining clearing, market access, and the role of intermediaries in derivatives markets. Chairman Selig delivered closing remarks, concluding AgCon2026. -CFTC-

items.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
items.summary: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says
items.summaryTr: Witnesses say a missile hit a building containing the surgical wards and intensive care units at Nasser hospital, the largest in southern Gaza.
items.articleText: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six Palestinians, health ministry says - Published Six people have been killed and about 30 injured in an Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in the southern Gaza Strip, the Hamas-run health ministry says. The hospital's director said two missiles hit a building containing surgical wards and intensive care units overnight, but that one of the missiles did not explode. The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions". The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces. Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime". Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war. Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies. Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory. The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people. In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department. Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion. The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded. "What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said. "Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital." Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts. News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile. Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion. "My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC. "I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all." He said he had been lying in a bed near Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, who was killed. Another colleague suffered a broken leg. "Dr Rizq was the kindest person in this department. He was very kind and always willing to help... And of course, he was a surgeon, one of the best among us." He added: "Patients were killed as well. There were patients in the rooms next to us who were killed. A patient comes to the hospital seeking treatment and leaves carried on people's shoulders. I do not know what kind of humanity this is." The Israeli military said in a statement that its "precise strike" had targeted the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, who it named as Mohammed Abu Ismail, alongside other fighters who were "hiding inside" Nasser hospital. "The terrorists were struck in order to remove the threat they posed after turning the Nasser hospital compound into a headquarters and operating from there to advance dozens of terrorist plots against our forces and restore the brigade's force," it alleged. The military added that it had issued advance warnings before the strike and released an audio recording of what it said was one given to a senior Gaza health official. But Fara insisted the hospital had received no warning of an attack. A Hamas statement rejected the Israeli military's accusations, calling them "a blatant attempt to justify a documented crime targeting a civilian medical facility whose function and purpose are well known". "The nature of the targeted site and the casualties inflicted on patients, doctors and medical staff expose the falsity and weakness of this narrative," it said. However, local activists circulated claims overnight that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building. Fara said this was the seventh time that Nasser hospital had been struck during the war. In August 2025, a double Israeli strike killed 22 Palestinians, including journalists and health workers. The World Health Organization (WHO) said it had documented a total of 1,056 attacks on healthcare in Gaza over the past three years, resulting in 1,010 deaths. "Gaza's health facilities are lifelines for its people. They must be protected. They must never be militarized or attacked," warned Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the UN agency's director general. Later on Thursday, at least four more Palestinians were reportedly killed in separate incidents in northern and central Gaza. Medics said three were killed in Israeli air strikes in Gaza City, Jabalia and Deir al-Balah, while the fourth was killed by Israeli gunfire in Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military said it struck a "terrorist" in Deir al-Balah and another in Gaza City. Israeli strikes on Gaza take place almost daily despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas in October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the same period. The humanitarian situation in Gaza also remains dire and has recently deteriorated further as a result of heavy rains last weekend that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says. - Published2 days ago

The health ministry said medical staff, patients and companions were killed, among them surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. It condemned the attack as a "flagrant violation of international laws and conventions". The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters who had used the hospital as a "headquarters" to plan attacks on its forces. Hamas said that Israel was spreading "false narratives" in a "blatant attempt to cover up a new war crime". Under international law, hospitals have a protected status, but they have been repeatedly targeted during the Gaza war. Israel accuses Hamas, which retains security control of parts of Gaza not occupied by Israeli troops, of cynically exploiting civilian infrastructure. It says the group stores weapons and runs command and control rooms in hospitals, which Hamas denies. Israel does not allow international news organisations, including the BBC, into Gaza, making it difficult to verify what is happening in the territory. The Nasser Medical Complex is located in the city of Khan Younis and is the largest hospital in southern Gaza, serving almost one million people. In a video posted on social media, a paramedic from the Hamas-run Civil Defence agency who arrived at the building after the strike early on Thursday said a missile penetrated the five-storey structure and hit a room in the surgical department. Other footage shared by activists showed thick smoke inside the building and extensive destruction on the second floor, where medical equipment and beds had been scattered by an explosion. The hospital's director, Dr Ahmed al-Fara, later told a news conference that Israeli forces had fired two missiles at the al-Yasin surgery building but that only one exploded. "What's happened in Nasser Medical Complex is targeting the health sector mainly. We are talking about doctors, we are talking about civilians, we are talking about patients," he said. "Also, there is... huge damage [to] the infrastructure inside the hospital." Footage filmed by a freelance journalist working for the BBC showed extensive damage to an operating theatre, wards and a sleeping area for medics, as well as hallways and lifts. News agencies also published photos that appeared to show an unexploded missile. Dr Mohammed Qdeih, a general surgery specialist who was wounded in the head, said he and other medical staff had just finished work around 00:30 and had been preparing to go to sleep when there was an explosion. "My whole body was trapped under the rubble. For a moment, I felt as if I was about to lose consciousness, or that I was about to die," he told the BBC. "I started struggling to free myself and started calling out, 'Guys! Guys!' I began crawling, trying to pull my leg out from beneath the rubble. I managed to pull myself free. It was dark, there were no lights, nothing at all." He said he had been lying in a bed near Dr Rizq Abu Shaira, who was killed. Another colleague suffered a broken leg. "Dr Rizq was the kindest person in this department. He was very kind and always willing to help... And of course, he was a surgeon, one of the best among us." He added: "Patients were killed as well. There were patients in the rooms next to us who were killed. A patient comes to the hospital seeking treatment and leaves carried on people's shoulders. I do not know what kind of humanity this is." The Israeli military said in a statement that its "precise strike" had targeted the commander of Hamas's Khan Younis Brigade, who it named as Mohammed Abu Ismail, alongside other fighters who were "hiding inside" Nasser hospital. "The terrorists were struck in order to remove the threat they posed after turning the Nasser hospital compound into a headquarters and operating from there to advance dozens of terrorist plots against our forces and restore the brigade's force," it alleged. The military added that it had issued advance warnings before the strike and released an audio recording of what it said was one given to a senior Gaza health official. But Fara insisted the hospital had received no warning of an attack. A Hamas statement rejected the Israeli military's accusations, calling them "a blatant attempt to justify a documented crime targeting a civilian medical facility whose function and purpose are well known". "The nature of the targeted site and the casualties inflicted on patients, doctors and medical staff expose the falsity and weakness of this narrative," it said. However, local activists circulated claims overnight that the strike may have targeted a senior Hamas security figure who was hiding inside the building. Fara said this was the seventh time that Nasser hospital had been struck during the war. In August 2025, a double Israeli strike killed 22 Palestinians, including journalists and health workers. The World Health Organization (WHO) said it had documented a total of 1,056 attacks on healthcare in Gaza over the past three years, resulting in 1,010 deaths. "Gaza's health facilities are lifelines for its people. They must be protected. They must never be militarized or attacked," warned Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the UN agency's director general. Later on Thursday, at least four more Palestinians were reportedly killed in separate incidents in northern and central Gaza. Medics said three were killed in Israeli air strikes in Gaza City, Jabalia and Deir al-Balah, while the fourth was killed by Israeli gunfire in Bureij refugee camp. The Israeli military said it struck a "terrorist" in Deir al-Balah and another in Gaza City. Israeli strikes on Gaza take place almost daily despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas in October last year. More than 1,620 people have been killed in Gaza since then, according to the territory's health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN. Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the same period. The humanitarian situation in Gaza also remains dire and has recently deteriorated further as a result of heavy rains last weekend that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents housing displaced families. The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage. Since then, more than 74,650 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says. - Published2 days ago

items.summaryTr: Golda Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. (GOLDA), 2025 hesap dönemine ilişkin kâr dağıtım kararını açıkladı. Yönetim Kurulunun kârın dağıtılmaması yönündeki teklifi Genel Kurulda kabul edildi.
items.articleText: Golda Gıda'dan temettü kararı: 2025 yılı kârı dağıtılmayacak - Golda Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. (GOLDA), 2025 hesap dönemine ilişkin kâr dağıtım kararını açıkladı. Yönetim Kurulunun kârın dağıtılmaması yönündeki teklifi Genel Kurul'da kabul edildi. Golda Gıda Sanayi ve Ticaret A.Ş. (GOLDA), 2025 yılı kârının kullanımına ve kâr dağıtımına ilişkin kararını Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) bildirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirket tarafından 12 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yapılan açıklamaya göre, Yönetim Kurulunun 2025 hesap dönemine ait kârın dağıtılmaması yönündeki teklifi Genel Kurul'da kabul edildi. Kararın, şirket esas sözleşmesinin "Kârın Tespiti ve Dağıtımı" başlıklı 20'nci maddesi, ilgili mevzuat ve Kâr Dağıtım Politikası çerçevesinde hazırlandığı belirtildi. GOLDA yatırımcıları için temettü kararı Genel Kurulda kabul edilen kararla birlikte Golda Gıda'nın 2025 hesap dönemine ilişkin kârından pay sahiplerine nakit temettü dağıtılmayacak. Temettü, şirketlerin elde ettikleri dönem kârının bir bölümünü nakit veya bedelsiz pay şeklinde ortaklarına dağıtması anlamına geliyor. Şirketlerin kâr dağıtıp dağıtmama kararı genel kurul onayından geçiyor.

items.title: Pentagon backs war memorial guard who reprimanded Hegseth's group
items.summary: The guard told the defence secretary and his companions to maintain an atmosphere of "silence and respect" during a Veterans Day visit.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: Pentagon backs war memorial guard who reprimanded Hegseth's group
items.summaryTr: The guard told the defence secretary and his companions to maintain an atmosphere of "silence and respect" during a Veterans Day visit.
items.articleText: Pentagon backs war memorial guard who reprimanded Hegseth's group - Published The Pentagon has given its backing to a US Army guard who reprimanded a group that included US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Arlington National Cemetery. A video of the Veterans Day observance event on Wednesday showed Hegseth, his wife, and senior advisers laughing and talking while posing for photos in front of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The footage showed the army sentinel on duty stepping towards Hegseth's group and shouting: "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times." Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said in a statement: "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum." "The Secretary and the entire Department have always honored - and will always honor - the sacrifices our military men and women have made to keep America safe." On Thursday, he presented an award to the soldier who reprimanded his group. Hegseth "welcomed the 3rd U.S. Infantry Regiment, the Old Guard to the Pentagon where he proudly awarded Specialist Thomas Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal for the execution of his duties at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier on November 11, 2026," the Pentagon said in a statement. In a post on X showing the soldier, Hesgeth said: "We love soldiers. We love standards. Well done, Specialist." The Arlington National Cemetery etiquette requests that visitors speak quietly and do not engage in disrespectful or disorderly conduct. The tomb, which is one of the country's most sacred war memorials, marks the final resting place of an unknown soldier who was killed in World War I. A service member from the 3rd Infantry Regiment stands watch over the tomb 24 hours a day and has done so since 1948. It is not unusual for them to admonish visitors to the site, according to the BBC's US partner CBS News. They reportedly do so a few times a day. Earlier, President Donald Trump, Vice-President JD Vance and other top officials attended the annual wreath-laying ceremony at the cemetery. During his speech at the ceremony, Trump offered his gratitude to uniformed service members who have fought for the country. He also touted what he sees as his administration's success in the Iran war. "Under this administration, and it was about time, somebody fought back. All of us fought back," he said. "And we won," Trump said of the Iran war. "It's just a question of when we want to end it. We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93% victory." Trump also pointed out Hegseth during the ceremony, saying he's done a "fantastic job" as defence secretary. Trump has repeatedly defended Hegseth amid Democratic lawmakers' push to impeach him. On Tuesday, an effort to impeach the defence secretary under accusations that he waged war on Iran without congressional authorisation failed on Capitol Hill. Hegseth has called the impeachment efforts a "farce" and a "stunt". Related topics - Published7 days ago

items.summary: Türk Telekom (TTKOM), 2029 vadeli kendi ihraç ettiği Eurobond'lardan 25 milyon dolar nominal değerindeki tahvili geri satın aldı. İşlem kapsamında ödenecek toplam tutar 26,1 milyon doları aştı.

items.titleTr: Türk Telekom'dan 26,1 milyon dolarlık Eurobond alımı
items.summaryTr: Türk Telekom (TTKOM), 2029 vadeli kendi ihraç ettiği Eurobond'lardan 25 milyon dolar nominal değerindeki tahvili geri satın aldı. İşlem kapsamında ödenecek toplam tutar 26,1 milyon doları aştı.
items.articleText: Türk Telekom'dan 26,1 milyon dolarlık Eurobond alımı - Türk Telekom (TTKOM), 2029 vadeli kendi ihraç ettiği Eurobond'lardan 25 milyon dolar nominal değerindeki tahvili geri satın aldı. İşlem kapsamında ödenecek toplam tutar 26,1 milyon doları aştı. Türk Telekom (TTKOM), kendi ihraç ettiği Eurobond'lara yönelik geri alım işlemi gerçekleştirdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Şirketin 12 Kasım 2026 tarihinde Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformu'na (KAP) yaptığı açıklamaya göre, 2029 vadeli tahvillerden 25 milyon ABD doları nominal değerinde alım yapıldı. XS2820499619 ISIN kodlu Eurobond'lar, 100,975 ABD doları fiyat üzerinden satın alındı. Toplam ödeme 26,1 milyon dolar KAP açıklamasında, söz konusu Eurobond'ların alım maliyetine kupon tahakkukunun da dahil edildiği belirtildi. İşlem kapsamında ödenecek toplam tutarın 26 milyon 145 bin 138,89 ABD doları olduğu bildirildi. Eurobond geri alımı, şirketlerin daha önce ihraç ettikleri ve piyasada işlem gören borçlanma araçlarını vadesinden önce yeniden satın alması anlamına geliyor. Bu işlemler şirketlerin borç yönetimi ve finansman stratejilerinin bir parçası olarak gerçekleştirilebiliyor.

items.titleTr: Ukraine says military Starlink disrupted again as US envoys meet Putin in Moscow
items.summaryTr: Later on Thursday, Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff will travel to Dublin to meet Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky.
items.articleText: Ukraine says military Starlink disrupted again as US envoys meet Putin in Moscow - Published President Volodymyr Zelensky has said Ukraine's military is again facing "systematic" restrictions to Starlink's military-grade satellite service, Starshield, meaning Kyiv is struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones. It came as US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after the latest talks aimed at ending the war in Ukraine wrapped up in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky told European leaders in Dublin that Ukraine was trying to clear up the Starlink situation with the American side. But he added "some things" were already clear: "If someone in America is making decisions that basically treat Ukrainian territory as if it is not Ukrainian, then this tells us where things are going." He did not elaborate further. Starshield was developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX company for government and military use. Along with Starlink, it has come to play a vital role in facilitating communication on Ukraine's front line. A similar issue with connectivity affected the front line in late October and lasted about a week before it was fixed. It remained unclear who had ordered the temporary restrictions on Starlink services at the time, with US officials and SpaceX offering differing explanations. Zelensky said the current disruption had been ongoing for several days and was "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians and carry out more accurate strikes against Ukraine". - Why is Ukraine so reliant on Starlink and can Europe plug the gap? - Published25 October Kushner and Witkoff are expected to travel to Dublin to meet Zelensky after their meeting with Putin. Videos shared by Russian media on Thursday showed the US representatives disembarking a plane and being welcomed by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev with handshakes and hugs. Later, they headed to the Kremlin where they met Putin and three of his senior advisors. In remarks broadcast by Russian media, Putin asked the US envoys to convey his "gratitude" to US First Lady Melania Trump for her involvement in last month's Kherson region ceasefire, which allowed for the evacuation of hundreds of civilians from the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky. The Russian president then proposed organising a similar five-day ceasefire for Kostyantynivka, a contested front-line Ukrainian city in the eastern region of Donetsk. Kyiv disputes that Russia fully holds the town, and a truce could help Moscow's troops to make a final push to seize it. "Considering that they brought in equipment and rotated troops in Oleshky under the guise of a humanitarian operation, it's clear what they want in Kostyantynivka," Ukrainian presidential adviser Dmitry Lytvyn said, adding that the details would need to be "clarified". The separate in-person meetings with the Russian and Ukrainian presidents were only announced on Wednesday after two days of talks which were framed as centred around the postwar security architecture of Europe. Nearly five years since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Moscow shows no sign of backing down from its maximalist demands for sovereign Ukrainian territory and for Western countries to give up any future commitment to protecting Kyiv in case of further attacks. On Thursday, Putin again repeated that the presence of foreign troops in Ukraine was "unacceptable" to Russia, and said Russia would like the Americans to engage with Europe "so that the Europeans can decide what they truly want: peace or war". During the first years of the war, Europeans cut communications with the Kremlin and refused to engage with Russia directly. However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table. The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture. Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations. But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle. Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses". However, in recent times many have grown concerned about the current US administration's commitment to European security and its softening towards the Kremlin, and have been pushing for a seat at the negotiating table. The talks in Abu Dhabi were led by the Americans and only included Russia and Ukraine, but Kushner said he and Witkoff would ask Putin to "give his blessing" to invite European representatives in future discussions - particularly with regards to the future configuration of their continent's security architecture. Kushner also urged Europe to "identify one person to speak on their behalf" in the negotiations. But the Russians have been opposed to the idea, citing Europe's support for Kyiv as an obstacle. Vladimir Medinsky, who headed the Russian delegation in Abu Dhabi, said he thought all parties had "moved closer to achieving peace" but that now "a lot depends on Ukraine, on the position of the United States, and on whether Europe comes to its senses". items.articleText: Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan COP31'de açıkladı: Türkiye'nin enerji hedefinde yeni adım - Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan, COP31 İş Forumu'nda Türkiye'nin yeşil dönüşüm hedeflerine ilişkin önemli mesajlar verdi. - Türkiye'nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefini yineleyen Erdoğan, "Nükleer güç santrallerimizin sayısını artıracağız" dedi. Erdoğan, iş dünyasına da iklim mücadelesinde daha fazla sorumluluk üstlenme çağrısı yaptı. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, COP31 İş Forumu'nda önemli açıklamalarda bulundu. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Erdoğan'ın açıklamalarından satır başları şöyle: "Dünya iş çevrelerinin kıymetli temsilcileri, saygıdeğer bakanlar, değerli misafirler. Sizleri en kalbi duygularımla, saygıyla, sevgiyle selamlıyorum. COP31 Liderler Zirvesi vesilesiyle sizlerle Antalya'da bir araya gelmekten büyük bir memnuniyet duyuyorum. Tarihin, tabiatın, tarımın ve turizmin buluşma noktası güzel Antalya'mıza hepiniz hoş geldiniz, sefalar getirdiniz. 96 lideri ülkemizde ağırladık Siyasetçiler, sivil toplum temsilcileri, çevre savunucuları ve iş dünyası olarak müşterek evimiz olan yeryüzünün geleceğine sahip çıkmak için Antalya'da toplanmış bulunuyoruz. Öncelikle Antalya'ya gelerek dünyamızı daha yaşanabilir bir yer haline getirme çabalarımıza verdiğiniz destek için her birinize teşekkür ediyorum. Türkiye Cumhuriyeti tarihinin en kapsamlı uluslararası organizasyonuna ev sahipliği yapmanın bahtiyarlığını yaşıyoruz. 9 Kasım'da başlayan COP31'de dün ve bugün yapılan Liderler Zirvesi'nde farklı unvanlarda 96 lideri ülkemizde ağırladık. 20 Kasım'a kadar devam edecek konferansa dünyanın dört bir yanından yaklaşık yüz bin kişinin katılımını bekliyoruz. Ön kayıt rakamlarına göre en yüksek katılımlı COP olmaya adayız. Yeşil ve mavi bölgelerden oluşan 1 milyon 100 bin metrekarelik alanımız şimdiye kadarki en büyük konferans alanları arasındadır. Bütün bu rakamlar konferansa verdiğimiz önemin yanı sıra ülkemizin çok taraflı diplomasisinin merkezlerinden biri haline geldiğini göstermektedir. Kıymetli dostlar, hepinizin bildiği üzere iklim krizinin ulaştığı ürkütücü boyutlar küresel ölçekte kararlı adımlar atılmasını zorunlu kılıyor. Bu anlayışta COP31'i taahhütlerin somut sonuçlara dönüşmesine imkan verecek bir uygulama konferansı olarak tasarladık. Liderler zirvemizin ilk gününü 'sıfır atık' konusuna ayırdık. Zirvemizin ikinci gününde ise 'dirençli şehirler ve sürdürülebilir çevre' temalarına odaklandık. Türkiye malumunuz 6 Şubat 2023'te asrın deprem felaketiyle sarsılmış bir ülkedir. 11 şehrimizi etkileyen bu felakette 53 binden fazla canımızı kaybettik. 6 Şubat depremlerinin ardından 3 yıldan daha kısa sürede 455 bin konut ve iş yeri inşa ederek deprem bölgemizi yeniden ayağa kaldırdık. Zirvede bu alandaki tecrübelerimizi katılımcılarla paylaşma imkanı bulduk. İklim değişikliğinin ağır etkilerine maruz kalan Afrika ve Pasifik ülkelerinin karşılaştığı zorlukları da gündeme taşıdık. Şunu burada bir kez daha altını çizerek ifade etmek isterim. Küresel karbon bütçesini tüketen gelişmiş ülkeler emisyon azaltımında ve finansmanda daha fazla sorumluluk üstlenmelidir. Gelişmekte olan ülkelerin kalkınma hakkı korunmalı, iklim krizinin bedelini en ağır ödeyen toplumlar güçlü biçimde desteklenmelidir. "Bunun bedelini evlatlarımız ödeyecektir" Ölümüzdeki günlerde müzakere başkanı Avustralya'nın da katkılarıyla belirlediğimiz 10 öncelikli alanda somut ilerleme sağlamayı hedefliyoruz. Ancak sizler de takdir edersiniz ki böyle evrensel bir mücadelede salt hükümetlerin gayretiyle başarıya ulaşılamaz. İş dünyasının da elini taşın altına koyarak sorumluluk üstlenmesi gerekir. Şurası bir gerçek ki bugün karşılaştığımız zorluklarda geçmişte çevreyi hoyratça kirletmenin, kaynakları hoyratça sömürmenin büyük payı vardır. 50 sene, 100 sene önce yapılan yanlışlar şimdi tek tek karşımıza çıkıyor. Eğer bugün biz de aynı hataları tekrarlar, ekolojiyi ekonomiye feda edersek bunun bedelini evlatlarımız ödeyecektir. Böyle bir yanlışa zaten biz izin vermeyiz. İş çevrelerimizin buna müsaade etmeyeceğine inanıyorum. Kıymetli misafirler, Türkiye olarak 2053 hedefimizi net sıfır emisyon olarak ilan ettik. Bu doğrultuda yeşil kalkınma yolculuğumuzu kararlılıkla sürdürüyoruz. Enerjiden sanayiye, ulaştırmadan tarıma ve binalara tüm sektörlerimizi yeniden yapılandırıyoruz. 2021 yılında hazırladığımız Yeşil Mutabakat Eylem Planımızla, kamu kurumları ve özel sektörümüzle birlikte yeşil dönüşüme yönelik kapsamlı bir yol haritası oluşturmuştuk. Önceki gün bu planı 2026-2030 dönemini kapsayacak şekilde yeniden güncelledik. Temel hedefimiz iklim değişikliği ile mücadele ederken sanayimizin rekabet gücünü artırmaktır. "Nükleer güç santrallerimizin sayısını artıracağız" Bu süreçte rüzgar, güneş, hidroelektrik gibi yeşil enerji yatırımlarını teşvik etmeyi sürdüreceğiz. Aynı şekilde nükleer güç santrallerimizin sayısını artıracağız. Her yıl on milyarlarca dolarını enerji ithalatına harcayan bir ülke olarak kendi kaynaklarımızı en üst düzeyde devreye almaya odaklanıyoruz. Elektrik kullanımının yaygınlaştırılması bir diğer önceliğimizdir. Gelecek 10 senede planımız en az %50 oranında artış sağlamaktır. Şu gerçeği inanıyorum ki bizi tanıyan, bilen, takip eden tüm dostlarımız çok net görüyor. Türkiye hayallerini hedeflere, hedeflerini gerçeklere dönüştürmede usta bir ülkedir. Hükümetlerimiz döneminde, son 24 yılda nice başarıya imza attık, nice zorluğun üstesinden geldik, nice badireyi suhuletle atlattık. Etrafımız yangın yerine çevrilmişken bugün de aynısını yapıyoruz. Ülkemizi çatışmalardan uzak tutuyor, bölgemizde barış ve istikrarın tesisi için samimiyetle çalışıyoruz. Fiyatlardaki aşırı yükseliş herkes gibi elbette bizleri de etkiliyor ama buna rağmen büyümeden, kalkınmadan, yeni yatırımlarla halkımızın refahını artırmaktan vazgeçmiyoruz. Türkiye bölgesinin istikrar ve güven adası konumunu son aylarda hem de çok güçlü biçimde teyit etmiştir. Uluslararası yatırımcıların ve kurumların Türkiye'ye güveni artarak devam etmektedir. Dünya Bankası'nın kredi portföyünde dünyada birinci sıradayız. Avrupa İmar ve Kalkınma Bankası'nda ise 6 yıldır zirvedeyiz. Bu sabah dört büyük Kalkınma Bankası'yla toplam 5,1 milyar dolarlık on anlaşma imzalandı. Bu kaynaklar inşallah çiftçimize, ihracatçımıza, kobilerimize ve ülkemizin kalkınma projelerine aktarılacak. Ancak şunu da hepimiz biliyoruz; finansman tek başına yeterli değildir. Asıl dönüşüm sizlerin vizyonuyla, sizlerin cesaretiyle, iş dünyamızın yapacağı yeni yatırımlarla gerçekleşecektir. Biliyorsunuz bunu savunma sanayinde başardık. Başka alanlarda da aynı başarıyı yakalamamız pekala mümkündür. KOP 31'in başarıyla düzenlenmesine katkı sağlayan herkesi, başta Murat Kurum kardeşimi tebrik ediyor, konferansın şimdiden hayırlara vesile olmasını diliyorum. Sağ olun, var olun, kalın sağlıcakla."

items.title: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
items.summary: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal
items.summaryTr: Within days, Huang's status as a seemingly untouchable figure leading the global tech race has crumbled.
items.articleText: The rise and fall of Jensen Huang - how the tech superstar became mired in scandal - Published Jensen Huang, known for sporting a black leather jacket to shareholder events, appeared to have it all. He was courted by leaders in both Washington and Beijing, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation. The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom. He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into free fall this week, undone by romantic entanglements, that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement. On Thursday he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman, alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague. His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China. Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg. But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips, which are used to power the new technology. The company, which is still valued at nearly $4 trillion despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses. Huang has had access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President XI Jinping. His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn (£109bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream. Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. The pair were lab partners and married in 1985, eight years before Huang founded Nvidia. They have two children, Madison and Spencer, who now both work at their father's firm. He worked at US chip firm AMD before co-founding Nvidia. Known as "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan, he has a reputation for having incredibly high standards for his staff. The company became a key provider of computer chips and circuits used for gaming before it expanded in direction and entered the world of AI. It now creates the key processing chips used to power the growing technology. Huang has hailed AI as a "new industrial revolution" that is on par with the advent of electricity. "Jensen Huang is a tech visionary of the likes of Steve Jobs," Stephen Witt, the author of Thinking Machine, a biography on the Jensen Huang, told the BBC, adding that he was responsible for creating AI hardware as we know it today. The Nvidia co-founder has a famously close relationship with Trump. At a recent AI summit at the White House, where 42 tech executives were present, the president was flanked by Huang and Musk. It was no surprise that Huang was at the top table. Companies using Nvidia's chips include Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic. In essence, Huang's customer base includes the biggest firms on the planet and they are spending plenty on Nvidia's products. This intertwining of companies means that the negative impact being felt by Nvidia, on the stock market for example, could perhaps have wider implications on other companies and the wider economy. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, and that it was "very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. But for someone who has gone to such great lengths to cultivate an image of being a family guy and who keeps his children very close, it is very bad." He was courted by leaders in both Washington and Beijing, worshipped by investors and seen as a loyal family man. But a rockstar approach to his personal life has ultimately led to his resignation. The 63-year-old has been married since 1985, long before the foundation of Nvidia, the company that propelled him to tech stardom. He is known as a workaholic and a demanding manager, with high standards for those who worked for him, which included his own children, promoted within the company. But he has seen his personal reputation go into free fall this week, undone by romantic entanglements, that throw doubt on his focus and his judgement. On Thursday he resigned following back-to-back revelations of two affairs. News of the first - a relationship with a businesswoman, alleged to be a Chinese spy - ricocheted around the world, raising eyebrows among investors. It was followed on Wednesday by reports that the tech boss had also had an affair with an Nvidia colleague. His departure creates uncertainty in the global stock market, which was already knocked-off balance in recent weeks. Nvidia is a linchpin in the US's race for technology leadership with China. Huang may not be a household name on the same level as Elon Musk or Mark Zuckerberg. But his role in the tech industry, especially in relation to the explosion of artificial intelligence in the last three years, may prove more consequential. Nvidia dominates the market for the microchips, which are used to power the new technology. The company, which is still valued at nearly $4 trillion despite recent events, is at the centre of the AI race between the US and China, the world's tech and economic powerhouses. Huang has had access to the seats of political power on an unrivalled scale, being courted by both US President Donald Trump and China's President XI Jinping. His remarkable rise to the top of his profession has led to him being dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and seen him amass an estimated fortune of $145bn (£109bn), according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. Despite always donning his trademark all-black outfits and playful approach to investor presentations, Huang has worked for years to present himself as a family man, someone who exemplified the American Dream. Born in Taiwan in 1963, Huang and his family moved to the west coast of the US when he was nine years old. He graduated as an electrical engineer from Oregon State University, and then with a master's degree in the same field from Stanford University. It was at college where he met his wife, Lori Mills. It was no surprise that Huang was at the top table. Companies using Nvidia's chips include Google, Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, SpaceX, Tesla, OpenAI and Anthropic. In essence, Huang's customer base includes the biggest firms on the planet and they are spending plenty on Nvidia's products. This intertwining of companies means that the negative impact being felt by Nvidia, on the stock market for example, could perhaps have wider implications on other companies and the wider economy. Witt told the BBC that Jensen Huang had gone to great lengths to present himself as a family man, and that it was "very important to him". "He praises his wife, he talks about her in very glowing ways," he added. "The fallout of this would be bad for anyone's family. items.articleText: Zorlu Holding'de yeni dönem: Yönetim Kurulu Başkanlığı'na yeni isim - Zorlu Holding Yönetim Kurulu Başkanlığı görevine Olgun Zorlu getirildi. - 1988'den bu yana grup bünyesinde farklı görevler üstlenen Zorlu, 2022'den itibaren Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili olarak görev yapıyordu. Zorlu Holding'in Yönetim Kurulu Başkanlığı görevine Olgun Zorlu atandı. Kasım ayı itibarıyla yeni görevine başlayan Olgun Zorlu, holdingin yönetiminde yeni dönemi üstlendi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Tekstil ve işletme alanlarında yüksek öğrenimini tamamladıktan sonra iş hayatına atılan Olgun Zorlu, 1988 yılından itibaren Zorlu Holding bünyesindeki şirketlerde yöneticilik yaptı. Görev aldığı şirketlerin yurt dışı pazar araştırmalarını ve yeni uygulama geliştirme çalışmalarını yöneten Zorlu, grubun farklı faaliyet alanlarında sorumluluk üstlendi. 1998'de yönetim kurulu üyesi oldu Olgun Zorlu, 1998 yılında Zorlu Holding Yönetim Kurulu Üyeliğine getirildi. 2022 yılında ise Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekilliği görevini üstlendi. Kasım 2026 itibarıyla Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı olarak görev yapmaya başlayan Zorlu, aynı zamanda Zorlu Grubu bünyesinde farklı sektörlerde faaliyet gösteren çok sayıda şirketin yönetim kurulu başkanlığını yürütüyor. TÜSİAD ve TETSİAD üyeliği bulunuyor Olgun Zorlu'nun iş dünyasındaki görevlerinin yanı sıra sivil toplum kuruluşlarında da üyelikleri bulunuyor. Zorlu, Türk Sanayicileri ve İş İnsanları Derneği (TÜSİAD) ile Türkiye Ev Tekstili Sanayicileri ve İş İnsanları Derneği (TETSİAD) üyesi olarak faaliyet gösteriyor. Zorlu Holding, tekstil, elektronik, beyaz eşya, enerji, gayrimenkul ve madencilik gibi farklı sektörlerde faaliyet gösteren bir şirketler grubu olarak öne çıkıyor. Olgun Zorlu'nun başkanlığa getirilmesi, grubun yönetiminde uzun yıllara dayanan deneyimin yeni döneme taşınması anlamına geliyor.

items.articleText: Washington'da Beyaz Saray yakınlarında silahlı saldırı: 1 ölü, saldırgan intihar etti - ABD'nin başkenti Washington'da Beyaz Saray'a yaklaşık 1,5 kilometre mesafede düzenlenen silahlı saldırıda 1 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 5 kişi yaralandı. - Polis takibine alınan şüpheli, bir binada barikat kurduktan sonra kendini vurarak yaşamına son verdi. ABD'nin başkenti Washington'da Beyaz Saray yakınlarında düzenlenen silahlı saldırıda can kaybı yaşandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Metropolitan Polis Departmanından yapılan açıklamaya göre saldırı, Beyaz Saray'a yaklaşık 1,5 kilometre uzaklıktaki Logan Circle semtinde meydana geldi. İlk belirlemelere göre saldırıda 5 kişi vuruldu. Metropolitan Polis Departmanı geçici şefi Jeffrey Carroll, olayda 1 kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini açıkladı. Saldırının ardından bölgeye çok sayıda polis ekibi sevk edilirken, çevrede geniş güvenlik önlemleri alındı. Olay yerine yakın okullar güvenlik gerekçesiyle kapatıldı, bazı yollar trafiğe kapatıldı. Saldırgan polis takibinin ardından intihar etti Metropolitan Polis Departmanı geçici şefi Jeffrey Carroll, şüphelinin polis takibinin ardından tespit edildiğini bildirdi. Carroll'un açıklamasına göre saldırgan, önce bir apartman dairesinde barikat kurdu. Daha sonra kendini vurarak yaşamına son verdi. İsminin açıklanmasını istemeyen bir emniyet yetkilisi ise saldırganın olayın başladığı spor salonunda en az bir kişiyi vurduktan sonra dışarı çıkarak ateş etmeyi sürdürdüğünü aktardı. Yetkili, güvenlik güçlerinin şüphelinin bir otopark asansöründe başka bir kişiyi vurduğunu ve ardından binanın 7'nci katında kendini kilitlediğini düşündüğünü belirtti. Görgü tanığı saldırı anını anlattı Saldırının başladığı spor salonunda bulunan James Spellman, saldırganın bir kişiyi boynundan vurduğunu ve bu kişinin olay yerinde hayatını kaybettiğini anlattı. Sosyal medyada paylaşılan görüntülerde ise silah sesleri duyulurken bölgede çok sayıda polis ekibinin bulunduğu ve çevredeki yolların kapatıldığı görüldü. Saldırı, Beyaz Saray'a yaklaşık 20 dakikalık yürüme mesafesinde bulunan Logan Circle semtinde gerçekleşti. Olayın nedeni ve yaralanan 5 kişinin sağlık durumuna ilişkin ayrıntılı bilgi henüz paylaşılmadı.
